scientific_use: Intersect genomic intervals to identify overlaps between CpG islands, exons, GWAS SNPs, enhancers/promoters, and chromatin states; use coverage fractions and Jaccard similarity to quantify regulatory overlap and compare random-shuffle expectations. Tutorial puzzles ask whether exons are wholly enhancer-overlapped, the fraction of GWAS SNPs in exons or regulatory states, and CpG similarity to enhancer/promoter intervals.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial composes existing bedtools commands (intersect, jaccard, shuffle and other shell utilities); it does not implement a new interval algorithm.

inputs.meaning: BED interval files: tutorial names cpg.bed, exons.bed, gwas.bed, hesc.chromHmm.bed, plus promoter/enhancer and tissue DNase tracks described in tutorial
inputs.format: BED; docs support BED/GFF/VCF and BAM inputs for intersect
inputs.stage: annotations, variant intervals, and peak calls; tutorial data source/version details incomplete

outputs.meaning: Overlapping records or base-pair overlap fields; Jaccard intersection/union similarity summaries; task-specific counts/fractions
outputs.format: tab-delimited BED-like output and tabular statistic

dependencies: bedtools CLI; shell pipelines; genome build and compatible interval coordinates; sorted inputs for -sorted workflows
Data assembly and exact promoter/enhancer sources must be resolved by author.
evidence: Tutorial explicitly defines intersect and examples for CpG/exon and multi-database overlaps; puzzles ask regulatory overlap and Jaccard questions.
Official intersect docs specify supported formats, overlap output controls, and presorted memory-efficient mode.
Official overview states tools can be piped into more complex analyses.
Tutorial ‘What are these files?’ gives dataset descriptions and sources.
limitations: Tutorial is historical (2017–2018); exact data files, assemblies, file access, versions, and licensing are unresolved.
Jaccard denominator implementation differs from textbook formulation per official docs; author must use documented bedtools definition.
No execution or grading behavior was tested.

scientific_use: Quantify read or feature depth and breadth over target intervals such as exons or fixed genomic windows, including strand-specific and properly paired read coverage. Output can support sequencing coverage assessment and target completeness analysis.
tool_role_basis: The documented workflow applies bedtools coverage/genomecov and optionally samtools to supplied alignments and intervals.

inputs.meaning: Target intervals (exons or genome tiling windows) and read alignments or other genomic features
inputs.format: BED/GFF/VCF/BAM; samtools-produced BAM stream also documented
inputs.stage: aligned sequencing reads and reference annotation; sortedness/coordinates must be compatible

outputs.meaning: Per-A interval overlap count, bases covered, interval length, fraction covered; optional per-position depth or histograms; genome-wide depth distribution

dependencies: bedtools; samtools for BAM filtering/conversion examples; genome reference/window definitions; sorted inputs and -sorted can reduce memory
Strand and paired-read filters alter the scientific definition of coverage.
evidence: Official coverage docs define depth, breadth, per-A output and supported formats.
Advanced usage docs compose bamtobed/samtools and coverage for exon, proper-pair and strand-specific coverage.
Tutorial describes genome coverage and asks counting exons in 500kb windows.
limitations: No BAM or complete genome data was inspected; no run-time claim is validated.
The tutorial’s genomecov example uses a large exon file and warns it may take several minutes; task sizing should use a small subset or explicit resource estimate.

title: Derive uncovered genomic regions and genome-wide coverage distribution

scientific_use: Use genome chromosome lengths and an interval set to derive the complementary uncovered regions (for example non-exonic genome), then quantify genome-wide coverage depth or breadth. Tutorial also asks for the genome regions neither exonic nor promoter-associated.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial applies bedtools complement and genomecov to annotation inputs; no algorithm implementation is requested.

inputs.meaning: Sorted genome feature intervals and chromosome sizes; optionally a second annotation set to subtract from complement

outputs.meaning: Intervals absent from input feature set within specified genome and genome-wide coverage histogram
outputs.stage: derived genomic regions and coverage summaries

dependencies: bedtools complement and genomecov; chromosome sizes for selected assembly; sorted intervals required by genomecov per tutorial
Need promoter intervals and exact assembly to reproduce the stated puzzle.
evidence: Tutorial explains complement as genome intervals not covered by input and requires a genome file.
Tutorial says genomecov reports genome-wide fraction by depth, requires sorted input and genome file.
Overview defines genomic features and documents the complement/genomecov tools.
limitations: The named genome file and its assembly are not fully specified in inspected tutorial excerpts.
The requested complement depends critically on genome boundaries and whether overlaps are merged before subtraction; task author must define this.
